analysis.investment_thesis: Caplin Point is the best business in this cohort by Magic Formula standards — ROCE of 25.8%, zero debt, and a staggering 26.2% revenue CAGR over 9 years — but an earnings yield of ~4.9% (EBIT INR 651 Cr / EV ~INR 13,290 Cr) sits just below the 6% threshold I require to pull the trigger. This is a near-buy: excellent ROIC, just not cheap enough yet.
key_strengths: ROCE of 25.8% and ROE of 22.7% — both above my thresholds — sustained over a 9-year compounding journey at 26% revenue CAGR
Debt-free fortress balance sheet (D/E 0.00, borrowings INR 5 Cr vs. equity INR 3,159 Cr) — zero financial risk, cash of INR 199 Cr
Operating margins of 31.4% in a generics business are exceptional — indicates genuine pricing power and manufacturing efficiency in LatAm niche markets
key_risks: Earnings yield of ~4.9% is below my 6% entry threshold — market has partially recognized the quality and the easy money has been made
High promoter concentration (70.57%) limits institutional float and can create liquidity/governance tail risks
US FDA entry (capex INR 192 Cr in FY25, CWIP INR 177 Cr) is a binary risk — regulatory delays or rejections could stall the next growth leg
red_flags: FCF in FY23 dropped to INR 78 Cr vs. INR 246 Cr in FY22 as capex ramped sharply — capital intensity is rising as the company targets US markets
Cash on hand dropped from INR 546 Cr (FY24) to INR 199 Cr (FY25) — large investing outflows absorbing the cash pile
Investing CF of –INR 333 Cr in FY25 relative to OCF of INR 432 Cr means FCF yield is lower than headline earnings suggest
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Caplin Point's Magic Formula profile is genuinely impressive: EV of ~INR 13,290 Cr (mkt cap INR 13,484 Cr + debt INR 5 Cr – cash INR 199 Cr) against EBIT of INR 651 Cr gives a 4.9% earnings yield — just below my 6% floor. ROCE of 25.8% clearly clears the 20% threshold. The 9-year compounding record (26% revenue CAGR, 31.5% net profit CAGR, margins expanding every year) is exactly the profile I look for: a company that earns high returns and then reinvests those returns at similarly high rates.

The knock is purely valuation — the market has started to price in Caplin's quality. At P/E of 21.9x the stock is not expensive in absolute terms, but for the Magic Formula to fire I need both legs simultaneously. The US FDA push could be transformative (TAM expansion) or dilutive (failed inspections, delayed approvals). If there's a market correction or earnings disappointment that pushes the stock down 15-20%, this crosses into clear buy territory. Today it sits in the 'watch closely' zone — the best quality in this group, waiting for the right price.
